title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary:
deep convolutional neural networks have led to a series of breakthroughs for image classiﬁcation . 
 deep networks naturally integrate low/mid/high-level features in an end-to-end multi-layer fashion , and the number of stacked layers ( depth ) can be enriched
by stacking more layers . on the challenging image recognition task 
 , the depth of representations is of central importance , and recent evidence reveals that network depth is of crucial importance .    in this paper 
 we present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used
previously . we explicitly reformulate the layers as learn-ing residual functions with reference to the layer inputs , in-stead of learning unreferenced functions . we provide com-prehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual
networks are easier to optimize , and can gain accuracy fromconsiderably increased depth .
key_findings: Deep residual networks improve image classification accuracy.
Residual learning framework eases the training of deeper networks.
Empirical evidence shows that deeper networks are easier to optimize.
methodology: The authors reformulate layers as learning residual functions with reference to layer inputs, allowing for deeper network architectures.
limitations: The study primarily focuses on image classification tasks.
The performance on other types of tasks is not evaluated.
future_work: Explore the application of residual learning in other domains.
Investigate the impact of residual networks on real-time image processing.
